recorded: Every case passed against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, tsx 4.23.1, @langchain/core 0.3.80, @langchain/langgraph 0.2.74, @langchain/openai 0.3.17, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0, express 4.22.2, and zod 3.25.76, run as "node --import tsx src/{program}.ts". The original always calls OpenRouter's address and the public status pages of GitHub and Cloudflare, so the copy that produced these cases reads OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPSPILOT_GITHUB_STATUS_URL, and OPSPILOT_CLOUDFLARE_STATUS_URL first and falls back to those addresses, a one-line change in the model factory and two in the status tool, and the cases point the status pages to the replay. No OpenRouter key was available, so the model answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gemma4:12b-mlx standing in for openai/gpt-4o-mini and without the stand-in's reasoning field, while the requests keep the model the program asked for. The status pages were recorded from the real ones on 2026-10-27, the failing page is synthesized, and the provider failure replays OpenRouter's documented error for a missing key. The chat server and the MCP server keep their SQLite database at data/opspilot.db, which each of their cases starts without and checks afterwards. Incident ids, conversation ids, latencies, and critique timestamps vary, so they are checked by shape, tool results that carry an incident id are checked by their call id only, and no case resolves an incident it has just opened. An MCP server may report invalid arguments and unknown tools as a tool result with isError or as a JSON-RPC error with code -32602, and validation errors are checked by their error code and a non-empty list of issues, because every validator words them differently. The arena's message about a missing key is checked by its first sentence, because the rest suggests Node.js commands.
